solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insight of person having special picture of a metropolis

parts.note: per is Latin for 'by' or 'for each', and here stands in for a person, as in 'per person'
pic is short for picture
a metropolis is a big city

explanation.surface: Someone's sharp insight comes from owning a special photograph of a great city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insight' is a mental quality, not a view of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacity is keen mental discernment, the ability to see into things clearly, which is what insight means.

clue.text: Distinguished artist has trouble with net

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: trouble means the word net is stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A distinguished artist struggles with a net.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist, often used for EMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in a field, distinguished.

clue.text: Disorganised carrier falls over

indicators.note: over means in this down clue one piece sits above the other

parts.note: slips means falls or trips
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A messy porter takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts SLIPS above HOD in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod means careless and untidy, disorganised.

clue.text: Lifting the lid on tablets for infections

indicators.note: lifting the lid means the top letter of the word for tablets is removed

parts.note: pills are tablets

explanation.surface: Opening a pill bottle to treat infections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting the lid' sounds like opening a container, but in a down clue it removes the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are ailments or troubles, of which infections are examples.

clue.text: Staggered by a hedonist's corruption

indicators.note: corruption means the letters of a hedonist's are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: here hedonist's is taken as all its letters, the S included

explanation.surface: People are shocked at how depraved a pleasure-seeker has become.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is used as a letter in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished and staggered both mean amazed, stunned with surprise.

clue.text: She gives directions to the taxman

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax authority
E, N and E are compass points, east, north, east

explanation.surface: A woman guides the tax inspector on his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue (IR) was the UK tax office before HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's name, so a 'she'.

clue.text: Unknown agent shot crossing the last river

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: crossing means one piece goes across another, so a letter sits inside the rearranged word
shot means the letters of agent are ruined into a new order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A secret agent of unknown identity is shot crossing the final river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges AGENT into ANGTE; 'crossing' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river.

clue.text: How loud noise and other disorder came at year one, some believe

definitions.text: How loud noise and other disorder came at year one, some believe

parts.note: a big bang is a loud noise

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of other are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cosmological account of how the universe began in noise and chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the cosmological model, while the pieces build it from a noise, a jumble of OTHER and a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang theory holds that the universe began from a hot dense explosion, as many scientists believe.

clue.text: Person ality

parts.note: the word personality is printed split in two, a split personality

explanation.walkthrough: Stevenson's doctor and his alter ego are the classic split personality, hence the broken word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde is the classic tale of one man with two selves, a byword for a split personality.

clue.text: The first E in Eileen

definitions.meaning: an adjective for what comes at the start
E is the opening letter of the name Eileen

explanation.definitionFit: Initial means coming at the beginning, and a person's initial is the first letter of a name, as E is for Eileen.

clue.text: Start to want extra effort now in everything from a pre-adolescent

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of each following word, from 'to' through 'everything', is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to a youngster: put extra effort into everything you want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' reads as 'begin to', but 'Start' is the instruction and 'to' is the first of the words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenie is a child between childhood and the teens, roughly nine to twelve years old, so not yet adolescent.

clue.text: Good Queen accepts Leicester's premier honour

indicators.note: accepts means the queen's name takes another letter into it

parts.note: Elizabeth I was popularly called Good Queen Bess

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letter of Leicester is used

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I grants the Earl of Leicester, her favourite, his foremost honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was Elizabeth I's favourite, so the surface is a historical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless can mean to glorify or confer favour on, which is to honour.

clue.text: Stock article on diocesans' core experiment

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: core means the central letters of diocesans are taken

parts.note: a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: A piece on a bishop's diocese tests its central matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Diocesans are people of a diocese; 'core' takes its middle three letters CES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of lineage or descent, a family line, is the same as ancestry.

clue.text: A little knowledge of affair to confess about

indicators.note: about means the confessing word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
a matter is an affair or business

explanation.surface: Someone admits knowing only a bit about an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing' is criminal slang for informing or confessing; 'about' wraps it round MATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, superficial knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Got on badly with a girl, but it'll be all right

indicators.note: badly signals the words got on are rearranged

parts.note: miss is a title for a young woman or girl

explanation.surface: He got on badly with a young woman, but things will be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got on badly' looks like a relationship report; 'badly' tells you to rearrange GOT ON into NOT GO.
explanation.definitionFit: If something would not go amiss it would be welcome or acceptable, so all right.

clue.text: Have a la carte selection of meat

indicators.note: selection of means some consecutive letters are picked out of have a la carte

explanation.surface: Order the calf meat from the à la carte menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu talk hides the letters across 'haVE A La'.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the meat of a calf.

clue.text: Jelly twice made from a fish

indicators.note: twice means the piece is written two times over

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A jelly made from a fish, cooked twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The gar, or garfish, is a fish with a long beak-like jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a setting agent for jellies.

clue.text: Something one takes up blowing amateurishly at first?

definitions.text: Something one takes up blowing amateurishly at first?

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of each of the four words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A beginner takes up an instrument and blows it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a brass instrument someone might start learning, while the initials of 'takes up blowing amateurishly' spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass instrument played by blowing, something a learner might take up.

clue.text: Mature plant turned to face endless wind

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for wind is dropped

parts.note: to blow is to move as wind does

indicators.note: turned means the word for the plant is read backwards

parts.note: moss is a small plant

explanation.surface: A grown plant swings round to face a strong wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective for the plant but is a verb; BLO and SSOM (MOSS backwards) join.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop and flourish, to mature.

clue.text: Build up some stress for engineer as a result

indicators.note: some means just part of the word stress is used, its first three letters

parts.note: then means consequently, as a result

explanation.surface: An engineer builds up stress in a structure as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes only STR from the start of 'stress'.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something is to fortify it, to build it up.

clue.text: Say who took some feeding, being given to escapism?

indicators.note: say signals the word who is pronounced and spelt to match

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like HOU

indicators.note: some means only part of the word for feeding is used

parts.note: dining is eating, feeding

explanation.surface: Who ate some of the food while seeking an escape?
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims DINING to DINI. The definition plays on escapism: the man was an escapologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the famous escapologist, someone devoted to escaping from chains and locks.

clue.text: English university invested in sticky sweet Cajun dish

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is put inside another, here a letter into the sweet

parts.note: toffee is a chewy, sticky sweet

explanation.surface: An English academic sinks into a sugary Louisiana dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts U inside TOFFEE, giving TOUFFEE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Étouffée is a Louisiana Cajun stew of shellfish smothered in a thick sauce over rice.

clue.text: Pretend to rule, wanting a fresh start

indicators.note: wanting a fresh start means the word for rule needs a different opening letter

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: Pretending to be in charge, needing to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued; the definition and crossings fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to fake or simulate, to pretend.

clue.text: Delinquent is thoroughly content

indicators.note: content means the letters contained inside the word thoroughly

explanation.surface: A young offender is completely happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'satisfied' but means the contents of 'thoroughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent, disorderly person, a hooligan or delinquent.

clue.text: How would Lester Piggott have stopped?

definitions.text: How would Lester Piggott have stopped?

parts.words: How would Lester Piggott have stopped?
parts.note: a famous jockey's call to halt his mount

explanation.walkthrough: Lester Piggott was a champion British flat-race jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command given to a horse to stop it.

clue.text: Composer is run out to boat in one

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
SS stands for steamship, a boat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A batsman is run out and sent off to row a boat on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'run out' when the stumps are broken before he reaches the crease; scorecards write it RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Old Whig is ridiculously OTT

indicators.note: ridiculously signals the letters of old whig are shuffled absurdly

explanation.surface: An old Whig politician behaves absurdly over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top', excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Going hog-wild means behaving with wild excess, completely over the top.

clue.text: Organise team inadequately, inviting third party involvement?

indicators.note: inadequately signals the letters of organise and team are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A manager arranges the team poorly and has to call in an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'third party' sounds like an outside helper, but the answer is a domestic arrangement for three.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a household arrangement in which three people share a sexual relationship.
